title: break and continue
learningObjectives: Explain break and continue and choose an appropriate control-flow structure.

understand.concept: break exits the nearest loop or switch. continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next iteration. In nested loops, these statements affect the nearest enclosing loop unless labelled statements are used.
understand.whyItMatters: These controls can simplify loops, but too many exits can make logic difficult to follow. Use them deliberately and keep loop conditions understandable.
understand.analogy: break leaves the repeated task; continue skips the current item and moves to the next one.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript control flow follows precise condition evaluation and iteration semantics.

explain.narrative: The loop skips 2, prints 1, 3, and 4, then exits when n is 5.

examples.explanation: The loop skips 2, prints 1, 3, and 4, then exits when n is 5.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the sequence or branch results described.

practise.guidedTask: Modify a loop to skip invalid records with continue and stop after a limit with break. Explain which iteration is affected.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the control-flow structure to process learner or course data. Test normal, boundary, and empty cases.
hints: Use strict comparisons for exact values.
Choose for...of for iterable values and avoid confusing keys with values.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>break and continue</title></head><body>
<script>for(let n=1;n<=6;n++){if(n===2)continue;if(n===5)break;console.log(n);}</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which statement skips the rest of the current iteration?
questions.explanation: continue moves to the next loop iteration without finishing the current body.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when writing a loop?
options: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.answer: That its condition and updates allow it to terminate as intended
questions.explanation: Correct termination and boundary handling prevent infinite loops and skipped work.
